title: Restart Strategies under a Known Mean (Las Vegas)
summary: Only the mean latency of a request is known. Bound the tail, work out what restarts guarantee inside a time budget, find the best number of equal attempts, show when restarting cannot help, and beat equal timeouts with unequal ones.
rubric: Part 1: the tightest bound on P(T > 5) that the mean alone gives, and a distribution that reaches it
Part 2: the guarantee of two 5-minute attempts against one 10-minute attempt
Part 3: the guarantee of N + 1 equal attempts for every N, with the distribution that makes it tight
Part 4: the number of equal attempts with the largest guarantee, and that guarantee
Part 5: a known distribution under which every schedule succeeds equally often, and why
Part 6: unequal timeouts: the best two-attempt schedule, what m attempts can reach, and how a known distribution changes the choice
